correctness.rationale: I reconstructed both bounds in the integer metric obtained by multiplying all unit-circumference distances by 4m. Choose s with 4s=m±1; a step-s edge has distance 4s, and square vertices of the same parity have distance either 0 or 2m. Both discrepancies are at least m−1. Thus distortion strictly below m−1 would force an alternating parity assignment along the step-s cycle, which is odd (in fact gcd(s,m)=1). This applies to any correspondence by selecting one square image for each vertex without requiring the selection to be surjective. For the four-block graph, same-block distances are ≤4k≤m−1; adjacent-label discrepancies are at most m−2 using source distances in [4,2m−2]; opposite-label pairs are separated in either direction by at least k+1 steps, so their discrepancy is ≤2m−4(k+1)≤m−1. The block sizes are positive for both residues, including m=5 and m=7. Undoing the scale multiplies distortion by 2π/(4m); halving distortion gives π(m−1)/(4m).
residual_risks: The recorded finite searches check single-valued maps only; the analytical argument, not those searches, excludes multivalued correspondences below the bound. No claim is made for chord distance.
